'''Tyrese John Haliburton''' (born February 29, 2000)<ref>{{cite web |title=HALIBURTON Tyrese |url=https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/athlete/tyrese-haliburton_1954705 |work=[[Paris 2024 Olympics]] |access-date=August 9, 2024 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240730141546/https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/athlete/tyrese-haliburton_1954705 |archive-date=July 30, 2024}}</ref>  is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Indiana Pacers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Nicknamed "'''Hali'''"<ref name=Chau/> and "'''the Haliban'''",<ref>{{cite web |last=Dennis Jr. |first=David |date=June 17, 2025 |title=Ball Up Top: SGA and J-Dub Takeover in Game 5, Hali Injured, Pacers Cooked? |url=https://andscape.com/features/ball-up-top-sga-and-j-dub-takeover-in-game-5-hali-injured-pacers-cooked/ |accessdate=June 19, 2025 |work=[[Andscape]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Price |first=Joe |title=Tyrese Halliburton: Why Are People Calling Pacers Star 'The Haliban?' |url=https://www.complex.com/sports/a/backwoodsaltar/people-referring-to-tyrese-haliburton-as-the-haliban |access-date=June 6, 2025 |website=[[Complex Networks|Complex]] |publisher=Commerce Media Holdings}}</ref> he is a two-time [[NBA All-Star]] and two-time [[All-NBA Third Team]] selection.

As a [[freshman]] playing [[college basketball]] with the [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State Cyclones]], Haliburton set the program's single-game [[assist (basketball)|assists]] record. He had breakout success as a [[sophomore]] and was named to the [[List of All-Big 12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big 12 Conference]] second team despite suffering a season-ending wrist injury.

Haliburton was selected by the [[Sacramento Kings]] 12th overall in the [[2020 NBA draft]]. In 2022, he was acquired by the [[Indiana Pacers]] as part of a trade package for [[Domantas Sabonis]]. Haliburton then earned back-to-back [[Eastern Conference (NBA)|East]] All-Star selections, being named to the All-Star team as a reserve in [[2023 NBA All-Star Game|2023]] and as a starter in [[2024 NBA All-Star Game|2024]]. In 2025, he led the Pacers to [[2025 NBA Finals|their first NBA Finals appearance in 25 years]].

In 2019, Haliburton helped the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States]] to a gold medal and earned all-tournament team honors at the [[2019 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|FIBA Under-19 World Cup]] in [[Heraklion]], Greece. He was also on the [[2024 United States men's Olympic basketball team|national team roster]] that won gold at the [[2024 Summer Olympics]] in Paris.

Haliburton has a younger brother, Marcel, from his parents' marriage, and two older brothers from his mother's previous marriage.<ref name="TrepelS043025">Trepel, Skyler (April 30, 2025). [https://people.com/all-about-tyrese-haliburton-parents-8671277  All About Tyrese Haliburton's Parents, John and Brenda Haliburton.] ''People''. Retrieved May 1, 2025.</ref>

Haliburton is biracial.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.essentiallysports.com/nba-active-basketball-news-what-is-tyrese-haliburton-s-ethnicity-tracing-indiana-pacers-star-lineage-and-family/|title=What Is Tyrese Haliburton's Ethnicity? Tracing Pacers Star's Lineage and Family|first=Meenu|last=Tomy|date=October 15, 2024|website=EssentiallySports}}</ref> His father is African-American and his mother is white.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.huffpost.com/entry/indiana-pacers-tyrese-haliburton-racial-slur-game-playoffs-nba_n_662960c0e4b01248ca9bc8ce|title=Pacers' Tyrese Haliburton Says His Brother Was Called A Racial Slur During A Game|date=April 24, 2024|website=HuffPost}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Sacramento Kings (2020–2022)===
====2020–21: All-Rookie honors====
Haliburton was selected with the 12th pick by the [[Sacramento Kings]] in the first round of the [[2020 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Kings Select Tyrese Haliburton in the First Round of the 2020 NBA Draft |url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-select-tyrese-haliburton-first-round-2020-nba-draft |date=November 18, 2020 |website=NBA.com |access-date=November 18, 2020}}</ref> On November 27, 2020, the Kings officially announced they had signed Haliburton.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kings Sign Tyrese Haliburton |url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-tyrese-haliburton |date=November 27, 2020 |website=NBA.com |access-date=November 27, 2020}}</ref> On December 23, he made his [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] debut, coming off the bench in a 124–122 [[Overtime (sports)|overtime]] victory over the [[Denver Nuggets]] with 12 points, four assists, two rebounds and a block.<ref>{{cite web |title=Hield tip-in leads Kings to 124–122 overtime win in Denver |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401267179 |date=December 23, 2020 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=December 23, 2020}}</ref> On April 14, 2021, Haliburton recorded a career-high six steals in a 123–111 loss to the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sactownroyalty.com/2021/4/14/22385071/sacramento-kings-drop-eight-straight-loss-washington-wizards-recap-final-score |title=Kings set new season-high in steals, but drop eighth straight |website=SB Nation |last=Rivas |first=Christian |date=April 14, 2021 |access-date=March 4, 2022 |archive-date=April 22, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230422052240/https://www.sactownroyalty.com/2021/4/14/22385071/sacramento-kings-drop-eight-straight-loss-washington-wizards-recap-final-score |url-status=dead}}</ref>

On May 2, 2021, Haliburton suffered a left knee injury against the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 5, 2021 |title=Haliburton's rookie season with Kings likely over |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31391487 |access-date=May 10, 2021 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> Although an MRI later revealed no ligament damage, it was announced that he would miss the last seven games of the Kings' [[2020–21 NBA season|2020–21 season]] as a precaution.<ref>{{cite web |last=Anderson |first=Jason |date=May 4, 2021 |title=Kings coach Luke Walton has good news and bad news about Tyrese Haliburton's knee injury |url=https://www.sacbee.com/sports/nba/sacramento-kings/article251155759.html}}</ref> After the season, Haliburton finished third in [[NBA Rookie of the Year|Rookie of the Year]] voting and was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie First Team]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/news/hornets-lamelo-ball-wins-kia-rookie-of-the-year |title=Hornets' LaMelo Ball wins 2020–21 Kia NBA Rookie of the Year |website=nba.com |date=June 17, 2021 |access-date=March 4, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/tyrese-haliburton-named-2020-21-nba-all-rookie-first-team/ |title=Tyrese Haliburton Named To 2020–21 NBA All-Rookie First Team |website=nba.com |date=June 17, 2021 |access-date=March 4, 2022}}</ref>

====2021–22: Final year in Sacramento====
On January 29, 2022, Haliburton scored his Kings' then-career-high 38 points along with seven assists, three rebounds and two steals in a 103–101 loss against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/kings/tyrese-haliburtons-career-high-38-points-wasted-kings-loss-76ers |website=NBC Sports |title=Haliburton's career-high 38 wasted in Kings' loss to 76ers |last=Thanawalla |first=Ali |date=January 29, 2022 |access-date=March 4, 2022}}</ref> Exactly a week later, in his final game as a King, Haliburton posted a then-career-high 17 assists, along with 13 points, six rebounds and two steals in a 113–103 victory over the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/kings/tyrese-haliburton-elite-company-career-high-17-assists-kings-win |title=Hali in elite group with career-high 17 assists in Kings' win |website=NBC Sports |last=Thanawalla |first=Ali |date=February 5, 2022 |access-date=March 4, 2022}}</ref>

With the trade deadline approaching, the Kings were seeking to acquire a center and held a surplus of point guards. The team had signed [[De'Aaron Fox]] to a five-year extension in 2020 to solidify him as the franchise's starting point guard, and later selected [[Davion Mitchell]] in the [[2021 NBA draft]]. As a result, Haliburton became Sacramento's best trade asset in efforts to immediately improve the roster and end an NBA-record 16-year playoff drought.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Salerno |first1=Cameron |title=Why the Kings traded away Tyrese Haliburton to the Pacers in one of the decade's most shocking moves |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/why-the-kings-traded-away-tyrese-haliburton-to-the-pacers-in-one-of-the-decades-most-shocking-moves/ |access-date=June 6, 2025 |work=CBS Sports |date=June 4, 2025}}</ref>

==National team career==
Haliburton played for the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States]] at the [[2019 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2019 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]] in [[Heraklion]], Greece.<ref name="peterson2">{{cite web |last=Peterson |first=Randy |title=Iowa State's Tyrese Haliburton makes USA's World Cup basketball team |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/iowa-state/randy-peterson/2019/06/20/team-usa-u-19-world-cup-tyrese-haliburton/1511411001/ |website=[[The Des Moines Register]] |access-date=June 30, 2019 |date=June 20, 2019}}</ref> On June 30, 2019, he scored a team-high 21 points, shooting 8-of-9 from the field, in a 102–84 group-stage win over [[Lithuania men's national under-18 and under-19 basketball team|Lithuania]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Haliburton Leads USA Past Lithuania |url=https://cyclones.com/news/2019/6/30/mens-basketball-haliburton-leads-usa-past-lithuania.aspx |publisher=Iowa State Cyclones |access-date=June 30, 2019 |date=June 30, 2019}}</ref> Haliburton averaged 7.9 points and a tournament-leading 6.9 assists per game while shooting 69 percent from the field. He led the United States to a gold medal and was named to the all-tournament team's [[FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup All-Tournament Team|All-Star Five]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Haliburton A Gold Medalist; Earns Spot On All-Star Five |url=https://cyclones.com/news/2019/7/7/mens-basketball-haliburton-a-gold-medalist-earns-spot-on-all-star-five.aspx |publisher=Iowa State Cyclones |access-date=July 7, 2019 |date=July 7, 2019}}</ref>

Haliburton was named to the 2021 USA Men's Select Team, working directly with the [[2020 United States men's Olympic basketball team|US Olympic Men's Basketball Team]] during training camp in [[Las Vegas]], Nevada prior to the [[2020 Tokyo Olympics]]. At the 2020 Olympics, the U.S. men's team was crowned [[Basketball at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|champions]] for the 16th time.<ref name="w407">{{cite web |title=Tyrese Haliburton Named To 2021 USA Men's Select Team |website=NBA.com |date=2021-07-01 |url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/tyrese-haliburton-named-2021-usa-mens-select-team |access-date=2025-03-02}}</ref><ref name="USA Basketball Notes">{{Cite web |title=USA Basketball Notes |url=https://www.usab.com/players/tyrese-haliburton |access-date=September 10, 2023 |website=USAB.com |language=en}}</ref>

Haliburton was selected to represent the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States Men's National Team]] at the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup]] in [[Pasay]], Philippines, at [[SM Mall of Asia Arena|Mall of Asia Arena]].<ref name="auto1"/> Across eight games, Haliburton averaged 8.6 points, 5.6 assists, three rebounds, 1.5 steals, 1.1 blocks, shooting 51% from the field and 47% from three-point range in 21.5 minutes per game off the bench. He led the team in steals and assists, helping the United States to a fourth-place finish that qualified the team for the [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics|2024 Summer Olympics]].<ref name="USA Basketball Notes"/>

Haliburton was later named to the [[2024 United States men's Olympic basketball team|2024 Olympic team]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Ben |last=Golliver |title=USA Basketball's gold medal formula: Big stars, bigger centers |date=July 10, 2024 |newspaper=The Washington Post |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/olympics/2024/07/10/usa-basketball-expectations-lebron-james-stephen-curry-kevin-durant/ |access-date=August 9, 2024}}</ref> He made his first Olympic appearance during a preliminary round win against [[South Sudan men's national basketball team|South Sudan]], recording six points and an assist on 2-3 three point shooting.<ref name=reynolds_07312024>{{cite news |first=Tim |last=Reynolds |title=US tops South Sudan 103-86 at Paris Olympics, earns spot in men's basketball quarterfinals |date=July 31, 2024 |publisher=The Associated Press |url=https://apnews.com/article/olympics-2024-south-sudan-us-basketball-741bde122a19cfdd435e427e4403ee73 |access-date=August 1, 2024}}</ref> Team USA would go on to win the gold medal in a rematch against [[France men's national basketball team|France]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://time.com/7009828/usa-france-gold/ |title=Team USA Men's Basketball Team Defeats France for Gold at Paris Olympics |website=time.com |last=Gregory |first=Sean |date=August 10, 2024 |access-date=November 11, 2024}}</ref>

==Player profile==
Haliburton is a point guard who stands {{convert|6|ft|5|in|m|2}}<ref>{{cite web|last=Jackson|first=Matthew|url=https://www.nbc.com/nbc-insider/who-is-the-indiana-pacers-tyrese-haliburton-everything-to-know|title= Who Is Tyrese Haliburton? Everything to Know About the Indiana Pacers' All-Star|publisher=[[NBC]]|date=June 5, 2025|accessdate=June 20, 2025}}</ref> tall and weighs {{convert|185|lbs|kg|0}}. Basketball writers have noted Haliburton as both an elite and high-volume three-point shooter.<ref name=Chau/> Despite this, Haliburton possesses a visually awkward shooting form described as "kooky"<ref name=Chau>{{cite web|last=Chau|first=Danny|display-authors=etal|url=https://nbarankings.theringer.com/rankings|title=The NBA, Ranked|work=[[The Ringer (website)|The Ringer]]|date=June 4, 2025|accessdate=June 20, 2025}}</ref> and "an almost embarrassing motion".<ref name=Thomas/> Louisa Thomas of ''[[The New Yorker]]'' detailed Haliburton's ability to "skitter past" defenders, before jerking into a quick shot characterized by an "[[wikt:akimbo|akimbo]]" right elbow set up by his use of "odd footwork, jabbing almost randomly".<ref name=Thomas>{{cite web|last=Thomas|first=Louisa|url=https://www.newyorker.com/sports/sporting-scene/tyrese-haliburton-has-worn-me-down|archive-url=https://archive.today/https://www.newyorker.com/sports/sporting-scene/tyrese-haliburton-has-worn-me-down|url-access=subscription|title=Tyrese Haliburton Has Worn Me Down.|work=[[The New Yorker]]|date=June 15, 2025|accessdate=June 20, 2025|archive-date=June 15, 2025}}</ref> 

Already the main distributor as his team's point guard, passing opportunities are further opened up for him due to his reputation as a perimeter threat.<ref name=Chau/> His Pacers teams, particularly in 2025, were known to play a considerably fast pace of play, with Haliburton directing their offense.<ref>{{cite web|last=Dominski|first=Michael|display-authors=etal|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/live-blogs/pacers-vs-thunder-live-updates-nba-finals-game-1-score-result/Limak465ue9Z/HBX1kor1mHXD/|url-access=subscription|title=Pacers stun Thunder in NBA Finals Game 1: Live updates and reaction from Indiana's win|work=[[The Athletic]]|publisher=[[The New York Times]]|date=June 6, 2025|accessdate=June 20, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Lewis|first=Ryan|url=https://www.beaconjournal.com/story/sports/pro/cavs/2025/05/05/nba-playoffs-cleveland-cavs-working-to-stop-pacers-tyrese-haliburton-donovan-mitchell-stats-schedule/83390288007/|title='They had us in the blender': Cavaliers must figure out how to stop Pacers in NBA playoffs|work=[[Akron Beacon Journal]]|date=May 5, 2025|accessdate=June 20, 2025}}</ref> In the [[2025 NBA playoffs]], after hitting multiple game-winning shots, analysts began to widely consider Haliburton as one of the most clutch players in the league.<ref name=Chau/><ref>{{cite web|last=Pina|first=Michael|url=https://www.theringer.com/2025/05/22/nba/indiana-pacers-tyrese-haliburton-new-york-knicks-game-1-nba-playoffs-2025|title=The Indiana Pacers Refuse to Die|work=[[The Ringer (website)|The Ringer]]|date=May 22, 2025|accessdate=June 21, 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Haliburton is a cousin of former basketball player [[Eddie Jones (basketball)|Eddie Jones]], who had a 14-year NBA career and was a three-time [[NBA All-Star]]. He is also the cousin of current [[Orlando Magic]] player [[Jalen Suggs]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nguyen |first=Gia |date=2025-06-17 |title=Are Jalen Suggs and Tyrese Haliburton Cousins? |url=https://www.sportscasting.com/news/are-jalen-suggs-and-tyrese-haliburton-cousins-magic-star-reveals-relationship-on-espn/ |access-date=2025-06-30 |website=Sportscasting {{!}} Pure Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> Haliburton has developed a friendship with [[Caitlin Clark]], a fellow basketball player in the Indiana market; Clark plays for the WNBA's [[Indiana Fever]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Shelburne|first=Ramona|author-link=Ramona Shelburne|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/45501463/nba-finals-2025-tyrese-haliburton-caitlin-clark-most-powerful-friendship-basketball|title=NBA Finals 2025: Tyrese Haliburton, Caitlin Clark and the most powerful friendship in basketball|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=June 13, 2025|accessdate=June 19, 2025}}</ref>

Haliburton is a [[Christianity|Christian]]. In 2024, he said, "My faith has grown a lot over the last year or two. Growing up we didn't go to church a lot, but we understood God's place in our lives. Now that I'm an adult I guess—I own a house now and live on my own—I go to church on Sunday every chance I can. I go to chapel before games."<ref>{{cite web |last=Mercer |first=Kevin |title=Pacers star Tyrese Haliburton advances to 1st NBA postseason as his 'faith has grown a lot' |url=https://sportsspectrum.com/sport/basketball/2024/04/17/pacers-tyrese-haliburton-1st-postseason-faith-grown-a-lot/ |website=Sports Spectrum |date=April 17, 2024 |access-date=April 24, 2024}}</ref>

Haliburton has been dating Jade Jones, who was a classmate of his and a cheerleader at Iowa State, since 2019. On July 28, 2025, it was announced that Haliburton and Jones got engaged.<ref name="engaged">{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/45844544/tyrese-haliburton-proposes-engaged-jade-jones-pacers|title=Tyrese Haliburton proposes to longtime girlfriend Jade Jones|first=Anthony|last=Gharib|website=ESPN.com|date=July 29, 2025}}</ref> They got married in August 2026<ref>{{Cite web |title=Instagram |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/Dbv3OYDlDZP/?img_index=1 |access-date=2026-08-10 |website=www.instagram.com}}</ref>
